# Results — Study 716 ("Short the diamond")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Lab-grown is killing the
natural diamond — can you get **paid** for it? We test the strongest tradable version of
the "short the diamond" pitch: a natural-diamond **price index** (hardcoded, cited,
**approximate** — a labelled proxy, not a live feed) and the only **listed** ways to
express the trade (the jeweler Signet `SIG`, the pure-play miner Lucara `LUC.TO`), each
benchmarked against `SPY`. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Price index | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** annual natural polished-diamond price level (base 100 @ 2018-12-31), reconstructed from public Rapaport RAPI / IDEX / Zimnisky / press reporting — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). **A PROXY, not a feed.** |
| Equity proxies | `SIG` (Signet Jewelers, NYSE) · `LUC.TO` (Lucara Diamond, TSX) — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| Benchmark | `SPY` (month-end Adj Close, yfinance) |
| As-of | 2025-12-31 (month-end; no partial-year bar) |
| Equity window | 2018-12 → 2025-12 (SIG/LUC.TO/SPY: 84 monthly returns) |

> **Why a proxy index, stated as a decision.** Real polished-diamond price indices
> (Rapaport's RapNet RAPI, the IDEX Polished Diamond Price Index, the Paul Zimnisky Global
> Polished Diamond Price Index) are **not freely API-available**. Rather than fabricate a
> live tape we (a) hardcode a small, clearly-cited, **approximate** annual series whose
> *shape* — a 2020–21 luxury-boom recovery, an **early-2022** peak, and a lab-grown-driven
> 2022–25 decline — is the load-bearing public fact, and (b) test the **tradable** equity
> proxies a public investor can actually trade. A jeweler's and a single-mine miner's
> equity are **not** the price of a polished stone; they are labelled proxies throughout.

## Half 1 — the diagnosis: are diamonds collapsing? (price index vs SPY)

The (approximate, cited) natural-diamond price index, year-end levels base 100:

| year | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| level | 100 | 94 | 96 | **118** | 122 | 104 | 92 | 90 |
| YoY | — | −6.0% | +2.1% | **+22.9%** | +3.4% | **−14.8%** | −11.5% | −2.2% |

The reported **peak was early 2022** (≈ level 132 on this scale); from there to the 2025
level the index **round-tripped −31.8%**. Headline risk/return vs SPY:

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Natural-diamond index** | **−1.49%** | 12.4% | −0.07 | **−26.2%** |
| SPY (year-end) | **+17.18%** | 16.9% | — | −18.2% |

**As a store of value, the diamond was a disaster** (−1.5%/yr vs +17.2%/yr for the S&P) —
which *confirms* the bear diagnosis. The mean annual excess (index − SPY) is **−19.3%/yr**,
**t = −2.30** (p = 0.061, n = 7 years). Read honestly, that *t* rides on a **hardcoded,
smooth proxy** series, so it certifies the *diagnosis* (diamonds fell), **not** a tradable
signal — a real noisy tape would print smaller, and "diamonds fell" tells you nothing about
how to get paid.

## Half 2 — the tradable proxies vs SPY (the only things you can trade)

Monthly Adj Close, Newey-West (6-lag) alpha vs SPY. **These are labelled proxies.**

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max DD | alpha/yr | beta | NW *t*(α) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SIG** (jeweler) | +17.05% | **66.2%** | 0.61 | **−77.8%** | +7.3% | 1.91 | +0.32 | 0.75 |
| **LUC.TO** (miner) | −24.27% | 49.6% | −0.32 | **−88.8%** | −26.0% | 0.82 | −1.73 | 0.09 |
| SPY | +17.18% | 16.6% | **1.04** | −23.9% | — | — | — | — |

Neither proxy clears a *significant* alpha (|t| < 2 both). Signet — the demand side — *rose*
with the market (β≈1.9, it sells lab-grown too); Lucara — the supply side — collapsed
**−85.7%** total, but with only *t* = −1.73 and as **one** mine's idiosyncratic story, not a
clean "diamond factor." **No harvestable diamond alpha, long or short.**

## Half 3a — "short the diamond": short the miner, net of borrow

The miner cratered — but a short is not free. Build a $1 short book on LUC.TO, earn −r each
month, pay a hard-to-borrow **30%/yr** fee (an illiquid $0.20 penny-stock):

| | value |
|---|--:|
| LUC.TO total return | −85.7% |
| short book, **no** borrow — CAGR | +1.91%/yr (only +13.9% total!) |
| short book, **net of 30%/yr borrow** — CAGR | **−22.59%/yr** |
| short book net — max drawdown | −93.5% |

The stunner: the miner **fell 86%**, yet a short book made only **+14% gross over 7 years** —
the +40%-plus up-months impose a vicious **volatility drag** (a short's payoff is concave in
the underlying). Charge the borrow and the whole thing goes **−22.6%/yr**. A perfectly
correct directional call that **lost money**.

## Half 3b — the physical stone: net of the retail→resale haircut

The "store of value" side never charges the round-trip: buy at **retail**, sell near
**wholesale** (~55% over a ~5-year hold), plus ~0.5%/yr carry. Charged once on the index's
gross CAGR:

| | value |
|---|--:|
| gross CAGR (index) | −1.49%/yr |
| − retail→resale spread drag (55% over 5y) | −14.76%/yr |
| − insurance/storage carry | −0.50%/yr |
| **= NET CAGR a real owner earns** | **−16.45%/yr** |

The resale spread alone is larger than a decade of any plausible appreciation. A diamond is
a consumption good priced like one.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic, fixed-seed "peak-and-collapse" path (planted boom CAGR +20%, bust −22%,
σ = 4.5%/mo, seed 716): the engine recovers the planted **down**-sign in the back half —
peak ≈ 201 → end ≈ 86, back-half CAGR **−17.0%**, full-window Sharpe −0.08, max DD −58.6%,
`sign_ok = 1`. The harness can bank a planted *collapse*, so a null on the real trade is a
real null, not a pipeline that can't see a trend.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No listed leg clears |t| ≥ 2 in the trade's favour (SIG *t* = +0.32,
  LUC.TO *t* = −1.73), and the short book loses net of borrow. The index's −19%/yr shortfall
  (*t* = −2.30) rides on a **hardcoded proxy** and certifies the *diagnosis*, not a
  harvestable signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Short LUC.TO net of 30%/yr borrow = **−22.6%/yr** (a −86% miner,
  and the short *still* lost — vol drag + borrow); the physical stone nets **−16.5%/yr** after
  the resale haircut. There is no diamond future, the pure-play short is a $0.20 penny-stock
  with no shortable float at size, and nothing scales.
- **Diamonds collapsing? — CONFIRMED.** Natural-diamond prices really did round-trip **−31.8%**
  off the early-2022 peak as lab-grown wholesale fell ~80–90%. The diagnosis is the
  best-supported part of the whole pitch — and the only part that's true.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The price index here is a **small, hardcoded, approximate**
> reconstruction of public reporting — its *shape* is defensible but its precise year-end
> values are not a live feed, and the annual *t* rests on 7 smooth observations (which
> *inflates* it). The equity proxies are exactly that — proxies for expressing "the diamond
> trade," and Lucara is a **single** surviving miner, so its path carries idiosyncratic risk
> that can't be read as diamond beta. Both limitations push the verdict toward humility: the
> collapse is real, the trade is not.
